semantic_correction.stem: The day after a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) procedure, a client develops new disorientation and asterixis. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: The findings are concerning for post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy and require prompt focused assessment and communication with the treating team.
options.B: The findings are a harmless expected effect of portal decompression and can be observed without evaluation unless they persist.
options.C: The findings prove the TIPS is occluded because hepatic encephalopathy occurs when portal decompression has failed.
options.D: The findings are best explained by routine venous-access discomfort and are unrelated to portosystemic shunting.

semantic_correction.rationale: AASLD identifies hepatic encephalopathy as a well-known complication after TIPS. TIPS diverts portal blood into the systemic circulation, decreasing first-pass hepatic clearance of neurotoxins such as ammonia and increasing the risk of encephalopathy. Current StatPearls guidance states that overt hepatic encephalopathy can begin with disorientation or asterixis and lists TIPS as a portosystemic-shunt cause. Hepatic encephalopathy remains a clinical diagnosis of exclusion, so the nurse should treat the new neurologic findings as concerning for post-TIPS encephalopathy, perform focused reassessment, and escalate rather than declaring a definitive diagnosis or assuming benign recovery. These findings do not by themselves prove shunt occlusion.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize new disorientation and asterixis after TIPS as possible post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy requiring prompt assessment and escalation.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item isolates a high-value post-TIPS complication, removes absolute distractor wording, and avoids falsely treating HE as proven without clinical evaluation.

option_audit.A: Correct. TIPS can precipitate HE, and disorientation plus asterixis are compatible with overt HE requiring prompt assessment.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. New neurologic changes after TIPS should not be dismissed as harmless routine recovery.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. HE can occur with a functioning TIPS and does not by itself establish shunt occlusion.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Venous-access discomfort does not explain a new mental-status change with asterixis.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A appropriately recognizes the likely complication while preserving the need to assess for alternative causes rather than claiming a definitive diagnosis.
cueing_check: All four choices are interpretations of the same postprocedure findings of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
